Review: I pay for it. Tl;dr I think the 14+ dollars I pay per month for Tinder Plus and Tinder Gold is worth the amount of time I sink into it.  So, long version. You get 100 swipes in a 12hr period for free. And that's cool if it's like a weekend or something or it's popping during the weekday. I will say that it is worth paying for if you care about having as many low effort convos that either lead to casual sex or something serious. There's nothing guaranteed, but casting the net wide is a wise idea, if you care. Let's say your goal is sex, but you're using the app for free. If you're a woman this really doesn't matter too much because people of any gender will swipe on women regardless of how they are in the looks department, I'm not sure too many people care about bios (I do because I'm a bit selective), but you can take this advice too if you are. Two words: SAMPLE SIZE. Maybe that's the wrong terminology - I'm not a math guy - but the point is whatever the population of the area using the app you are broadcasting in will determine the ratio. Layman's terms: Chicago has like 3 million people. Assume at least 200,000 people are using the app at the same time. That's 1:200,000. If you only have 100 swipes, there is a HIGH chance you will BOTH not get a match on your end (swiping) and not be seen. When you pay for Tinder Plus, you get infinite likes for a month ( you get other stuff too I think, look it up). And that's really cool. However that doesn't solve the problem completely. You still don't know who has swiped on you. Remember, it takes two for this to work ( not to mention you can't message people directly on Tinder.). That problem is solved with Tinder Gold (sounds like a meme, right? Well it ain't). With Tinder Gold you can see who likes you already, swipe on them, and voila you've got a match! As an added bonus, with the Boost option that you get it will broadcast you on every single Tinder app within whatever mile radius you prescribe thereby increasing your visibility. Think of it as putting you to the top of the stack. I've met, smashed, and dated a bunch of girls here that I probably otherwise wouldn't have without it (I don't do so great in social settings, but I have no anxiety online.). So, uh, yeah, try it out or whatever and look things up for yourself because I'm 90% sure I'm forgetting a few things lol

I have a better idea Tinder, I'll remove the app, delete my account, and find a more reasonable service.  You're not the only game out there Tinder. Already this makes people who are willing to pour money into the app the only ones who will be seen, because if 100 people in a 6 mile radius use boosts and youre not the sort of person to swipe through 100 people per hour, then you will never encounter a person who hasnt paid for the app with the exception of some serious luck.  Consider this: Scenario 1) You yourself use a boost,  many people of your preferred sex (this is bad for both men and women straight or gay trust me) start noticing your profile and you get a large amount of likes, unfortunately, many of these likes will likely come from people who havent used boosts so you will never encounter them.  Scenario 2) You dont use a boost, but you still start swiping because you still want to try, everyone you swipe right on will not see your profile because they will have to dig through everyone who is using a boost. Boosts wear off after half an hour, fine, but if you live in a heavily populated area the odds of a large amount of people using boosts one after the other increases dramatically, meaning you could potentially never see a non-boosted member.  I dont have the statistics to prove these scenarios are in effect, but if someone is willing to use tinder in current year, then theyre probably willing to pay five bucks to boost themselves.  Tinder staff need to see if this is a real issue. Tinder has over 100 million downloads, this app seriously affects peoples lives and relationships nowadays, Tinder needs to take responsibility and fix this 'non-boost' void.

Review: Has a simple interface that is easy to use, and it's free to communicate. A rather pricey subscription fee unlocks additional features, none of which seem worth the cost. You can't communicate with someone, nor they with you, unless you match, which means you both "swiped right" on each other's profile. Since communication is predicated on "swiping right" and the initial physical attraction, most people don't seem to put much in their profiles, and I believe this is the bad side of Tinder. A couple of sentences or sometimes nothing. I encountered many profiles where they only put an email or kik id. Many, many fake profiles and photos. The few contacts I had turned out to be fake or scammers. You get the standard fake messages from scammers, "How long have you been here and what are you looking for? I live in the US but I am currently in (insert country) visiting family or going to school or working." My favorite is when they live in another part of the country but just happen to be in a nearby town on vacation, and they ask for your contact information. You can tell they just picked a random town off a map. Could be a great app. Maybe it is if you are in a large city. But watch out for scammers and fakes, people trying to get your contact information, people with motives other than actually looking for a relationship. Based on my experience, I give it one star.

You also only see who the message is from, you have to go to the app to read the actual message. Video chat would also be nice I guess, and an indicator of how many likes I have left (non-paying user). Review: Ok so this review has everything to do with the app itself and NOTHING to do with the people on it.  The app is set laid out in a way that even the most computer illiterate people should quickly be able to figure it out. You simply upload a few pics, have the option to input a few details about yourself (including job title, a short bio, age) and then you input your settings to tell the app who youre looking for (men, women, both + an age range and how far youre willing to travel to meet up) the app then shows you whos available in your area with a snapshot view of each users profile, you simply swipe left or hit the X button if youre not interested, OR if you like what you see you can swipe right (or up for "super like") or hit the heart button (or star button for the super like option). As youre swiping, the app will notify you when someone has swiped right on your profile as well, and it will notify you that you have a match. Now that youve matched, you have the option to privately message each other. This explaination might be kind of lengthy but the set up process takes 5 minutes and matching just depends on how attractive you are tbh. Good luck out there folks!!

Tl;dr is that nothing about it is free anymore, and entirely centralised around paid monthly subscriptions and overpriced consumables. Name: Android Testerer
Review: Tinder is the dating app that changed the way we view dating apps: each day you are presented with 30 or so images of other users, either female or male (of your choice) who have recently used the app and who are within a specified proximity to you. You anonymously 'like' or 'pass' on these images. Each image shows the users Facebook name (the app requires a Facebook account and mobile phone number verification to use) as well as their profession/school as specified in Facebook. By tapping on the user's image, you can see more images of the user (if they added more), their exact distance from you, as well as an up-to-500 character profile text (if they chose to write one). You HAVE to 'like' or 'pass' on a profile when presented with one: you cannot skip to other profiles without making a judgment. Should both users secretly 'like' each other, the 'match' is revealed to both users and then both users can then message each other for free. Sadly, the 'game' style of Tinder often equates to 'less than serious' users who match but then never talk, or those who match and then 'unmatch' immediately. Regardless, of all the match-game-dating-apps out there, this one is the original n best.
